# Artifacts and Extended Memory

## Paper as mind

> status: ratified (D-0028)

Every paper artifact in this world — the rare bound book, the oracle deck, the meanest
scrap — is an extension of human memory and reasoning power. This is the organizing
idea of the material culture: things are valuable in proportion to the thinking they
can hold. It also grounds the cooperative theme: minds linked through shared artifacts
out-reason any solitary genius ([[magic-system]]).

## The time-blurred inventory

> status: ratified (D-0026, D-0042)

The deliberate anachronism of the setting: tapestries and cartomancy (a tarot/oracle
equivalent) exist alongside genuinely rare, expensive books — while the economy stays
strictly medieval and there is no electricity or engine-power of any kind. Their
medicine holds real concepts (infection, anatomy) executed with moss, boiled water,
and bone saws. To a modern eye the technology is ragged, mixed-period, human-scale —
and everywhere under pressure from the ruling order's cheap standardized goods
([[economy]]).

## The deck

> status: ratified (D-0146, D-0148, D-0180)

The world's oracular deck is **the Turning** ([[the-turning]]) — its own tradition, not our
tarot. It began as a commons reckoning-game and turned to counsel; a reader lays its painted
leaves to hold the moving parts of a problem still, freeing working memory for the argument
itself. Decks are personal, worn, annotated, and a reader's spread-habits are as identifying as
handwriting. Enfys's own deck is painted on scraped vellum in soot-and-bog-berry ink, the
imperial-trained defector re-learning the folk hand; the deck's full structure — its Grounds,
Hands, Weathers, and the Reckoner — lives at [[the-turning]].
Within the single proof-system architecture, a deck is a reconfigurable premise map
and counsel tool. It can support proof-work by making premises walkable, but it does
not predict or cast.

## The loom and the knot

> status: provisional (D-0072, D-0180)

Weaving, knitting, and knot-work are the deep records of the native cultures. A
tapestry is an archive; a knot-string is a saved argument; a birthing-girdle is a
small, temporary ward spoken into fiber by someone's hands. Because the empire polices
parchment, the resistance's most important documents hang on laundry lines and wrap
shivering children, illegible to the bailiffs who requisition them. "Women's work" is,
quietly, the world's most complete library ([[womens-lives]], [[information-control]]).
The approved architecture fixes the direction: knots and woven records are holders,
timers, archives, and local constraints for proof, not a separate rope-magic system.

## The book

> status: provisional (D-0072)

Books are rare, costly, and — in the present age — mostly instruments of the ruling
order: bound, fixed, mass-copied law that does not adapt to the valley it lands on.
The native traditions distrust the bound page not out of superstition but out of
experience; the far-future orders remember that distrust ([[religion]]). A book is not
evil. A book is a very large claim, permanently asserted.

## Ogham, scraps, marginalia

> status: provisional (D-0072)

Between loom and book lives the small stuff: tally-notches on the edge of a stick
(the Ogham-like edge-script of the old cultures), stolen vellum offcuts carrying one
hard-won premise each, marginalia traded at hedge-fairs like currency. A saved theorem
on a scrap can be the difference between a village's ward holding or failing.

## Craft as embodied memory

> status: ratified (D-0042)

Beyond paper: knowledge lives in hands. Lost crafts, and crafts one bad winter from
dying out, are a central preoccupation — the smith's strike-rhythm, the herbwife's
nose, the drover's read of a sky. Preserving and rediscovering these human-scale arts
is both plot engine and theme, set against the ruling order's push to standardize
everything into cheap, disposable sameness.

## Divination as counsel

> status: ratified (D-0146)

Card-reading and its kin are counsel, never prophecy. A reading is a tool for the
mind that holds it — premises laid out where the eye can walk them, the same
extended cognition as the knot and the woven record — and what it returns is a
better question, not a fixed future. This keeps divination inside the world's
epistemology (the Wyrd is not fate) and inside the craft register: a reader is
skilled the way a joiner is skilled, and a bad reading is bad work, not bad luck.
